newsitem.title: PERU: Peru names five bidders for La Oroya mining sale.
newsitem.headline: Peru names five bidders for La Oroya mining sale.

text.p: Five foreign mining firms were set to bid at next week's auction of Peru's huge La Oroya metallurgic complex, state miner Centromin said Monday.
Centromin said the three latest firms to announce their intention to bid were Switzerland's Glencore International, Spain's Asturiana de Zinc and Brazil's Paranapanema.
Mexico's Industrias Penoles S.A. and the United States' Doe Run Co had already said they would bid.
The five companies will present their technical credentials April 14 and offer their financial bids April 18, when the auction winner will be announced, Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares said.

Centromin has set a $70 million minimum bid price for the auction, whose terms oblige the winning firm to immediately inject the money offered at the sale into the complex as capital and then invest a further $120 million over the next five years.

La Oroya lies in the country's central Andes 12,300 feet (3,700 meters) above sea level and 120 miles (190 km) east of Lima. The complex of refineries and smelters La Oroya is Centromin's largest asset, processing 22 metals and their byproducts.
